title: Fire Breaks Out at Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith’s $42 Million Calabasas Estate — Shed Burns, No One Hurt
excerpt: A fire broke out early Monday at Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith’s $42 million Calabasas estate. A shed burned; firefighters put it out. No one was hurt.
content:
A fire broke out early Monday morning at the $42 million Calabasas estate of Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith, burning a maintenance shed on the couple’s 150-acre property before firefighters put it out. No one was hurt.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department said deputies from the Malibu/Lost Hills Station responded at about 12:04 a.m. on Monday, November 23, to a report of a structure fire on the 1400 block of Cold Canyon Road in Calabasas. Security at the property reported a maintenance shed was on fire, and deputies arrived to find the shed engulfed in flames. Los Angeles County Fire Department crews extinguished the blaze. In 911 dispatch audio obtained by Page Six, a firefighter reported a shed on fire with no spread to the brush, and the call was downgraded to a structure fire.

The sheriff’s station told Page Six that no other structures were damaged, no one was injured, and the cause of the fire was accidental. It was not immediately clear whether Smith, 58, or Pinkett Smith, 55, was at the property when the fire broke out, and representatives for the couple did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Not the first fire at the estate

This is not the first fire at the couple’s home. In 2021, a fire broke out in the basement of the main house, and the property later underwent renovations. Smith bought the land for the Calabasas compound in 2003. The couple, married since December 1997, were seen together on Saturday in Malibu with their children and both of their mothers in a rare family outing, just two days before the fire.

What it means

Analysis: the speed of the response is the story here. A shed fire reported just after midnight was contained before it could reach the main house or the surrounding brush — in a region where a single ember can become a wildfire, that is the best possible outcome of a bad night. The open question is what sparked the shed fire, and whether the couple was home when it happened.
